data.title: Why Is Oracle Stock Falling in Pre-Market Today, Sept. 15?
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) stock is down by 1.24% in premarket trading today. The company has reportedly started another round of job cuts as it continues to spend heavily on AI infrastructure. Business Insider reported that the layoffs were expected to start Monday, citing affected employees and an internal notification email. Workers reportedly began receiving notices that their positions were being eliminated as part of a broader organizational change.

What Oracle Told Employees in Its Latest Layoff Email

"After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organisational change. As a result, today is your last working day," the notice said, according to a copy reviewed by Business Insider.

Reports began surfacing on social media early Monday that some Oracle employees were unable to access company systems, including email and Slack. For many workers, the loss of access appeared to signal that their jobs had been cut.

Promotion

Explore ORCZ for 2X short leverage on ORCL

Several former Oracle employees also shared details in a LinkedIn thread. They said layoff notices were not sent to their personal email accounts, leaving some workers unsure about their status. Some had to contact their managers, while others had already been told that their roles were at risk.

Under the severance plan, affected employees were reportedly offered four weeks of base salary, plus one additional week for each year they had worked at Oracle.

Another Round of Layoffs

The latest layoffs follow job cuts Oracle made earlier this year. The company's workforce fell by about 21,000 employees, or 13%, during the fiscal year ended May 31, according to a recent filing.

Oracle's latest quarterly SEC filing shows that the company is increasing its 2026 restructuring budget by another $700 million. Before the end of the quarter, Oracle had expected restructuring costs of up to $2.1 billion, mainly related to employee severance, contract termination fees, and other exit costs.

The higher restructuring budget comes as Oracle reported $19.3 billion in revenue for Q1 FY27, which ended August 31. The results show strong growth as Oracle continues to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. However, the company is also cutting jobs and raising spending on restructuring as it adjusts its workforce and business costs.

Is Oracle a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

On TipRanks, ORCL stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 26 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Oracle price target of $251.52 implies over 70% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, ORCL shares have dropped 25%.

data.title: The Space Race Is Heating Up — and One Analyst Says Buy These 2 Stocks
data.description:
Once upon a time, the 'space race' meant the grand strategic competition between the USA and the USSR to gain control of the heavens. The superpowers designed and built satellites, manned capsules, orbital spacecraft and long-endurance space stations, and NASA even sent the Apollo landers to put men on the Moon.

Today, the space race is heating up again, but in a very different way. Yes, the governments are still involved – NASA's Artemis program is targeting the Moon, the Russians have a Soyuz escape ship docked at the International Space Station, and other powers such as the EU, China, and India have large-scale space programs. But the real difference – and a lot of the innovation – is coming from commercial players working alongside government space agencies.

This past summer, Elon Musk's SpaceX went public, in Wall Street's largest ever IPO. The company is pioneering reusable large rockets, and has already made history with privately launched and/or publicly funded missions of the Falcon 9 rocket and Crew Dragon capsule.

Promotion

Explore ASTX for 2X leverage on ASTS

SpaceX is only the largest of a growing cadre of private space launch companies, however. Smaller firms are sending up satellites, designing new rocket technologies, and generally shaking up the industry. As Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov said earlier this month, "Falling launch costs have enabled a rapidly growing investable universe in which we want to own the bottlenecks and differentiated downstream applications. The collapse in launch costs has driven the space economy past $500bn in 2025, and is on track to exceed $1trn by 2030. Near term, defence and sovereignty budgets provide de-risked demand while commercial markets scale, and we believe pricing power sits with the few proven high cadence launch providers, though longer term, value migrates downstream to applications that scale at little marginal cost. We favour vertically integrated launch and differentiated/sovereign constellation capability that cannot easily be replicated."

Filatov goes on to recommend that investors buy two space stocks – companies that will benefit in a hotter space race. We've opened up the databanks at TipRanks to get a close look at them; here are the details, and Filatov's comments.

Rocket Lab USA (RKLB)

Rocket Lab, the first stock on our list of Berenberg picks, is a ~$37.5 billion space launch firm, with a proven, reusable, small-payload rocket available for customers, a deep work backlog, and a leading position among commercial launch firms in the low Earth orbit (LEO) niche. The company specializes, for now, in deploying reusable launch vehicles to send small payloads into orbit – a key capability, as it helps to populate the growing satellite constellations that are circling our globe.

Like any successful company, Rocket Lab has built its business around the needs of its customer base. It provides vital launch services for companies in such fields as satcom, communications, and imaging, and has also become an important contractor for various government agencies. All of these customers have their own idiosyncratic needs – but Rocket Lab's rocket tech can facilitate their disparate payloads.

The company's main tool right now is the Electron rocket, one of the space industry's most-used launch vehicles in the US market. The Electron, which can loft a payload up to 300 kilograms, has made 95 launches to date, including 16 in 2026. Rocket Lab operates 3 launch pads, and boasts that Electron's flights have put over 265 satellites safely into orbit.

Rocket Lab's other vehicles include a test bed project, dubbed HASTE, for Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron. HASTE is designed to test suborbital, high-speed systems, and can carry a 700 kilogram payload. The company has another project in late-stage development, the Neutron rocket, which is designed to loft large-scale payloads, up to 13,000 kilograms, into low Earth orbit. The rocket's specs even include an interplanetary launch capability, for sending 1,500 kilogram payloads to Mars or Venus. We should note, however, that Rocket Lab has recently pushed back the planned first launch of the Neutron; where it had been planned for later this year, the company now says that the first Neutron will be delivered to the launch pad during 4Q26, with the launch set for early next year. Like Electron, Neutron is designed to be a reusable vehicle.

Also of note for Rocket Lab, the company reported a record-level work backlog at the end of 2Q26 – totaling $2.36 billion and up 137% year-over-year. This is a clear indication of both Rocket Lab's solid work offerings and the general expansion of the private space launch industry.

In that Q2 report, Rocket Lab's revenue was also reported as a record – and at $234 million, the top line was up 62% year-over-year and beat the forecast by over $3 million. At the bottom line, Rocket Lab is running a net loss – not uncommon with leading-edge tech-related companies – but the GAAP EPS of ($0.08) represented an improvement over the 13-cent per share loss reported in 2Q25. The 2Q26 bottom line was in line with expectations.

Analyst Filatov, in his write-up here for Berenberg, notes that Rocket Lab has a strong business model, a sizable backlog to fall back on, and a quality catalyst in the near future. He writes, "We view vertical integration across launch, manufacturing and applications as the most valuable combination in space, carrying optionality not reflected in the headline multiple. With launch a clear industry bottleneck visible in preflight Neutron dedicated bookings and Electron backlog, upside to space systems estimates from the programme pipeline, a broad range of growth avenues in applications and a founder-led team that has repeatedly proven its ability to execute and expand its addressable market, we believe Rocket Lab is perhaps the most compelling and differentiated long-term asset to own in the space sector, particularly as its closest public peer, SpaceX, increasingly aligns itself with the AI theme. We acknowledge the execution risk and extreme multiple and would buy/add on volatility."

The Berenberg expert's take on Rocket Lab is clearly bullish, and his comments back up the Buy rating, while the $83 price target implies a one-year upside potential for the stock of 33%. (To watch Filatov's track record, click here.)

RKLB shares have a Strong Buy consensus rating from the Street, based on 17 recent reviews that include 14 Buys to 3 Holds. The stock is priced at $62.55, and its $110.13 average target price indicates an even more bullish upside than Filatov suggests, at 76%. (See RKLB stock forecast.)

data.title: Bloom Energy Stock (BE) Can Shrug Off AI Slowdown Fears
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE), at first glance, has an obvious reason to worry investors when artificial intelligence (AI) stocks sell off. This is because its fuel cells are closely tied to data center power needs. After AI executives called for a slower pace of development over the weekend, Bloom Energy opened deep in the red on Monday. Yet Bloom maintains strong momentum, with Q2 revenue growth of 166%. It entered the year with roughly $20 billion in backlog.

After all, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says his proposal does not mean "halting model training." I believe the market is mistaking caution about tomorrow's models for cancellation of power projects already in motion. Thus, my BE forecast is bullish.

For context, Bloom Energy is a clean energy company that manufactures solid oxide fuel cell platforms to generate reliable, on-site electricity for power-intensive facilities like AI data centers.

data.title: AI Slowdown Debate Lifts Software Stocks as MNDY Jumps 10.7%
data.description:
Enterprise software stocks rallied Monday as investors considered an unusual question: Could slower AI development actually be good for software companies? ServiceNow, Inc. (NOW) climbed 7.41%, Salesforce, Inc. (CRM) rose 4.73%, Monday.com Ltd. (MNDY) jumped 10.67%, and Figma, Inc. (FIG) gained 3.06%.

The move came as the debate over the pace of AI development intensified. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called over the weekend for slowing advances in frontier AI models, with other major AI industry leaders also backing greater emphasis on safety. That debate appears to have briefly reshaped one of the market's biggest AI trades.

data.title: Stock Market Today, September 15 – Futures Slip as Treasury Yields Cross 5%, Rate Hike Looms
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell ahead of Tuesday's session as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.03%, while oil prices continued to rise amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. Investors are awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Markets are pricing in a 92% probability of a 0.25 percentage-point rate hike, which would lift the Fed's target range to 3.75%-4.00%.

Futures on the Nasdaq 100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 0.63%, 0.55%, and 0.67%, respectively, as of 5:38 a.m. EDT on September 15.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as fresh attacks in the Gulf raised concerns about supply disruptions. Saudi Arabia also shut its key East-West oil pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, after drone attacks damaged it, further tightening supply. At the time of writing, Brent crude (CM:BZ) rose to $108.88 a barrel, while WTI crude (CM:CL) was near $104.03 a barrel.

data.title: OpenAI Buys $300M Glass Imaging Startup as AI Hardware Push Expands
data.description:
OpenAI has acquired Glass Imaging, a smartphone camera startup valued at more than $300 million, according to The Wall Street Journal. The purchase gives OpenAI technology designed to use AI to produce smartphone images closer to DSLR quality and adds to its growing push into consumer hardware.

Glass Imaging was founded in 2019 by former Apple employees Ziv Attar and Tom Bishop, who previously worked on camera technology at Apple (AAPL), including portrait mode. The startup was valued at about $100 million in a funding round last year, meaning the OpenAI deal values the company at more than three times that level.

The company had raised about $30 million from investors including GV, Alphabet's venture arm, and Insight Partners. Its zoom-imaging technology has also appeared in smartphones from Honor.

data.title: Trump Rejects Tighter AI Regulation as Nvidia, Big Tech Face AI Slowdown Risk
data.description:
President Donald Trump pushed back against calls for tighter AI regulation on Monday, arguing that new federal guardrails could slow the U.S. technology industry and give China an advantage. His comments put Washington's AI policy back in focus as investors weigh whether rising safety concerns could eventually affect spending on chips, data centers, and other AI infrastructure.

Trump said on Truth Social that additional AI controls could drive companies toward "oblivion and bankruptcy." During a call with Nvidia Corporation (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang, Trump also defended the expansion of AI and data centers, describing the technology as potentially bigger than the internet.

The comments come as some of the industry's most prominent executives are calling for more caution. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has argued for slowing the development of the most advanced AI systems, while OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has backed a federal framework with consistent safety requirements. Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) has also published a provisional code of conduct for training new AI models.

Promotion

Explore AMZO for 2X short leverage on AMZN

AI Spending Is the Market Question

The growing tension is especially important for Nvidia and other AI-linked companies because slower development could eventually reduce the need for the enormous computing capacity required to train and run advanced models.

That spending reaches well beyond chipmakers. Microsoft, Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta Platforms (META) have been investing heavily in AI computing and data-center capacity. A federal policy that keeps restrictions relatively light would remove one potential obstacle to continued expansion, although Trump's comments do not guarantee that AI spending will remain at current levels.

However, Wall Street has not abandoned the AI trade despite the latest safety warnings. Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta shares each gained about 2% or more on Monday, even as investors debated whether the industry's rapid development should slow.

data.title: Bank of America Stock (BAC) Drops on Weak Q3 Outlook — Is a Broader Slowdown Coming?
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) shares fell 5% on Monday after CEO Brian Moynihan warned that its Wall Street businesses could see a weaker third quarter. Speaking at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference, Moynihan said investment banking fees could fall more than 10% year-over-year in Q3 to $1.6 billion-$1.8 billion, while trading revenue is expected to be roughly flat. The outlook is a sharp change from Q2, when Bank of America reported a 50% jump in investment banking fees and a 33% increase in trading revenue.

BAC was the weakest-performing stock in the KBW Bank Index on Monday. Other major bank stocks also fell, with Goldman Sachs (GS) down about 4.1% and Morgan Stanley (MS) down 3.6%, while Citigroup (C) fell 2%.

Is a Broader Wall Street Slowdown Coming?

BofA's weaker outlook may be more than a company-specific issue. Data from Jefferies (JEF) suggests that investment banking activity was already slowing across major banks before BofA issued its warning. As of Sept. 3, investment banking revenue at eight major global banks was down 15% from a year earlier and 27% from Q2, according to Jefferies data.

Still, not all banks may feel the impact equally. Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) could be better positioned because of their broader investment banking businesses and strong positions in M&A and equity capital markets. This gives them more ways to offset weakness in any one area.

On a positive note, Moynihan pointed to a strong deal pipeline, especially in middle-market investment banking, offering some optimism for future activity.
